label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
The Winter School on Elliptic Curves and Modular Forms ended on Saturday, and I'm still catching up on sleep. We ran it from 5 to 7 November in Seminar Hall 2, Department of Mathematics, Sahyadri Institute of Science, Pune.

Some numbers for context: we got 112 applications and selected 41 MSc and early PhD students from 9 states, based on a statement and one reference. A Rs 2.4 lakh grant from the institute's student initiative covered hostel stay and travel for 18 outstation students.

Thank you to our speakers for three days of great teaching. Dr. Nilesh Dharmadhikari (Hyderabad) took us through Mordell-Weil, Dr. Sunanda Iyer (Chennai) taught modular forms, and Dr. Tomasz Wierzbicki joined online from Kraków for computations in Sage. One of our MSc students from Silchar spotted an error in a worked example in Sunanda ma'am's notes. She corrected it live and thanked him, which was great to see.

Thank you to Prof. Anuradha Venkatesan, our faculty mentor, for backing a student-run school and guiding us throughout. Thank you to Mr. Prakash Salunke from the office, who sorted out our hostel rooms at 11 pm when the booking got messed up. Thank you to the 6 PhD students who volunteered as TAs and ran the problem sessions. That format worked really well and we will keep it. And thank you to my co-organisers Ketaki Joglekar and Faizan Mirza, and to all 41 participants for the questions and the energy.

On the afternoon of day 2, the power went out for nearly two hours and the laptops died. We moved the problem session to the canteen with two rolling whiteboards, and it turned out to be the best session of the three days.

I believe small schools like this matter more than big conferences for MSc students, because they actually get to sit down and ask questions. That's why we want to do this again.

We hope to run a second edition in late 2027, though it depends on whether the grant comes through. Slides and problem sheets will go up on the department website in about two weeks, and I'll share the link here when they do.

Thank you, everyone. It was a lot of work and well worth it.
